extracted.intended_audience: prospective students, applicants to university/medical school courses and academic job applicants (early 20th-century UK)
extracted.subtask_description: Compilation of higher-education course notices, entrance and appointment requirements, and application instructions for universities, medical schools, and technical colleges (UK). Primarily for prospective students and applicants for academic/teaching posts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entrance requirements — University College Hospital Medical School
rubrics_metrics.description: A student may enter the School as soon as he has passed the University of London Matriculation Examination, or one of the other Preliminary Examinations that Qualify a Medical Student for entering a Medical School.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a student has only matriculation he will pursue Preliminary and Intermediate Studies at University College and then carry on advanced Medical Studies at the Hospital. A student who has completed Preliminary and Intermediate Medical Studies elsewhere may enter for advanced Medical Studies only. Qualified medical men and others who can produce evidence of sufficient qualifications may be admitted to Special Departments for research, or to Hospital Practice for certain definite periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical appointments and selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Thirty-six Clinical Appointments, eighteen of which are resident, are filled up by competition during the year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These appointments, as well as clerkships and dresserships, are open to students of the Hospital without extra fee. (Context: competitive selection for clinical posts.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees and payment options for medical courses
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees for courses are specified (e.g., Final M.B. Course at University College Hospital Medical School: 80 guineas if paid in one sum, or 82 guineas paid in two instalments of 50 and 32 guineas).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prospective students should note published course fees and payment options when applying; prospectuses supply full details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application/prospectus access and contact for course details
rubrics_metrics.description: Prospectus, with information as to Classes, Scholarships, &c., may be obtained from the Dean or Secretary (addresses given).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full particulars and forms of application can be obtained by writing to the named Dean/Secretary; some notices instruct applicants to send stamped addressed envelopes to receive forms or particulars by post.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application timing for research laboratory admission (Davy–Faraday Laboratory)
rubrics_metrics.description: To prevent delay Candidates ought to send in their applications a few months preceding the Term in which they wish to enter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full information and forms of application can be had from the Assistant Secretary, Royal Institution; early submission recommended to avoid delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner and assistant-master appointment requirements (County of London)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appointments as examiners (for degrees in Arts, Science, and Medicine) and as Assistant Master are advertised with specified qualifications and duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: For Degrees in Arts, Science and Medicine, one examiner (Natural Philosophy including Practical Physics) should be qualified both on the Mathematical and Experimental side. Appointments are for three or four years from January 1. Salaries for examiner posts are given (e.g., annual salary figures listed). Candidates must lodge copies of their application and testimonials with the Secretary by stated deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headship appointment requirements — Selby Secondary School (Head Mistress)
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates must hold a degree or its equivalent, and must be trained or have had suitable teaching experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must be made not later than the stated date, and not more than three recent testimonials should be sent with the application. 'Canvassing will be a disqualification.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Overseas technical/teaching appointment requirements (Board of Education, Auckland / Auckland Technical College)
rubrics_metrics.description: Science and Mathematical Master: candidates will be required to teach Physics, Chemistry, and Elementary Mathematics; successful teaching experience essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Salary and terms noted (e.g., £250 per annum), engagement for at least three years, and passage paid. Full particulars and application forms obtainable from the High Commissioner; applications must be received by the stated deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application materials and testimonial rules (general pattern across notices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Most appointments and competitions require submission of application forms accompanied by testimonials; some specify the maximum number of testimonials and require copies to be lodged with a named official (Secretary/Registrar).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Candidates should lodge two copies of their application and testimonials with the Secretary...' and 'not more than three recent testimonials must be sent with the application.' Deadlines and addresses are given; failure to follow specified submission procedure may invalidate applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti-pattern: canvassing as disqualification
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit rule in at least one advertisement: 'Canvassing will be a disqualification.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants for advertised school/headship posts must not engage in canvassing; doing so may render the application invalid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course content and practical training expectations (Statistical and Biometrical Laboratory)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Laboratory provides a complete course of training in both the theory and practice of Statistics, including instruction in exhibition, calculation (mechanical and arithmetical), and use of statistical quantities; advanced students assisted in research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lab open daily with stated hours; fees and terms for lectures, practical work, and research students are given (e.g., lectures £6 6s per session; practical work £6 6s; research students £5 5s per term). Prospective students should note the practical equipment (mechanical integrators, calculators) and the research assistance available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special-course and laboratory research access
rubrics_metrics.description: Several notices state that laboratories are open for research and that special facilities are given for those desiring to engage in research (e.g., Electrochemistry, Practical work in Chemistry and Metallurgy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants interested in research should enquire for 'Special facilities' and apply to the named departmental secretaries; some courses specify that laboratories are open to students for practical work and research.
